name: chad-review
description: 6-pass autonomous pre-commit code review: drift, behavior-and-risk, tests, observability, dependency-freshness, and simplification, over uncommitted working-tree changes or the last commit if the tree is clean. Runs the project's own deterministic gate before any agent launches, and a repo with no validation entrypoint is itself a finding with a ready-to-paste target. Dependency freshness is a script rather than a prompt: it finds manifests, lockfiles, pinned versions, version-bearing references in files that are not manifests, and undeclared prerequisites, so doc, prompt, and IaC repos get audited instead of marked N/A. It cross-checks what the vulnerability scanner actually read against what it discovered, so an ecosystem nothing scanned is reported as a coverage gap rather than passing for clean, and it scans lockfiles that .gitignore hides from the scanner's own walk. Findings are grouped by the upgrade that closes them, so one bump fixing nine advisories reads as one decision. Diff-shape aware, one reviewer per language block, session-relative sonnet/opus tiering with an explicit model on every launch. NOT read-only: it never edits the change under review and never commits, but it executes your gate, tests, codegen, linters, and vulnerability scanner, all of which write to disk, and it backs up untracked files first because the no-edit rule is prompt-enforced rather than tool-enforced.
